solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Punish, in this case wrongly

indicators.note: arranged wrongly, so the letters of the phrase are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone decides that in this particular case the punishment handed out was a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges THIS CASE; 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to discipline or rebuke someone, a synonym for punishing them.

clue.text: On a ship, comprehensive direction-finder

definitions.note: a ... shows the direction of magnetic north

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another goes above it, so the school comes first

parts.note: a comp is short for a comprehensive, a British state secondary school
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Aboard ship, the all-round instrument for finding the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehensive' looks like an adjective but is a noun: in Britain a comprehensive is a state secondary school taking all abilities, shortened to comp.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass shows magnetic north, so it is the instrument used to find direction.

clue.text: A short test in lobbies

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the test is removed

parts.note: a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A brief exam held in entrance halls.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is an entrance hall or central court of a building, so atria are lobbies.

clue.text: Standard menu elated both going out

indicators.note: going out as in going out of their places, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A set dinner thrills two people about to go out for the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Table d'hote is a fixed-price set meal with limited choice, a restaurant's standard menu.

clue.text: After treatment, stay in normal frame of mind

indicators.note: the words have been processed and reworked, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hospital stay restores a patient to their right mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanity is soundness of mind, the healthy, rational state of thinking.

clue.text: A service returned from a distance

indicators.note: something returned comes back, so the letters of this service are read backwards

parts.note: the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone returns from military service, coming back from far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' is the reversal signal, though in the surface it reads as coming home from service.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar is an adverb meaning at or from a great distance, as in 'seen from afar'.

clue.text: Delivers one a flower

parts.note: to deliver someone is to free them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A florist sends someone a single bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The freesia is a fragrant flowering plant from southern Africa, popular in bouquets.

clue.text: Bank holding a sort of race

indicators.note: the outer word holds the other inside it

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A financial institution sponsors a running event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is a verb, to count on, not a financial institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A relay is a team race in which each runner covers a leg in turn.

clue.text: Bone in heap, not quite dead?

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, so the bone goes inside the heap

parts.note: a mound is a heap or pile
a rib is one of the bones of the chest

explanation.surface: A bone lies in a pile of remains, and the question is whether its owner is truly dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: moribund means close to death rather than literally almost dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Moribund describes someone on the point of dying, which is about as near to being dead as one can be while still alive.

clue.text: Lock up penguin killer

definitions.meaning: the leopard ... of Antarctica is a notorious predator of penguins

explanation.surface: Someone wants a bird-killing predator put behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to close tightly, and the marine mammal of the same name preys on penguins.

clue.text: The first recipe, perhaps, for track sport

parts.note: a recipe is one example of a formula, a set method or mix of ingredients
the first in a sequence is number one

explanation.surface: Someone sets out the very first recipe for an athletic event.
explanation.definitionFit: Formula One is the top class of motor racing, run on circuits, so it is a sport on a track.

clue.text: Lower a foot

parts.note: the base of something is its foot or bottom part

explanation.surface: An instruction to bring something down by twelve inches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is a verb here, to humble, not 'less high'; 'foot' is the bottom, not the measure.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase someone is to lower or degrade them in dignity or rank.

clue.text: Revolutionary is wrong to back heaven

indicators.note: to back is to go backwards, so the letters of the legal wrong are read in reverse

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
the sky is the heavens above

explanation.surface: A rebel is told that backing the cause of heaven is a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wrong' looks like a verdict, but 'wrong' is TORT, which 'to back' reverses to TROT; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Trotsky was a leader of the Russian Revolution of 1917, so he is a famous revolutionary.

clue.text: Small lake in view

indicators.note: the lake is placed in the view, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sight is something seen, a view
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A little lake comes into view.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight is a synonym of small, slender or minor, as in a slight figure or a slight chance.

clue.text: A script: it's about girl underground, mostly

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, so the girl sits inside
most of the name, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: Alice, whose story was first titled Alice's Adventures Under Ground

explanation.surface: A screenplay about a girl living below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl underground is Lewis Carroll's heroine, who fell down the rabbit hole; the apostrophe in 'it's' is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Italics are a sloping typeface, one style of script or lettering used in print.

clue.text: Almost transfix a native of Africa

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so the last letter of the synonym for transfix is dropped

parts.note: to impale is to pierce through, to transfix with a spike

explanation.surface: Someone nearly spears an African local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts IMPALE to IMPAL, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an antelope found across southern and eastern Africa, so it is an African native animal.

clue.text: Organise a run over some mountains

indicators.note: in a down clue, the run sits over, that is above, the mountains

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: An instruction to plan a hill race.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange something is to set it in order or plan it, to organise it.

clue.text: Other ranks row about a decree

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: the noise goes around the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a din is a row, a loud noise

explanation.surface: Enlisted soldiers argue over an official order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is a noisy racket here, not a line or a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to order or establish by authority, which is to decree.

clue.text: Turncoat's characteristic: wanting gold

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic feature
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: The defining feature of a defector is his greed for gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Turncoat' stands for 'is', and 'wanting' (needing) is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat is someone who betrays their side, which is exactly what a traitor does.

clue.text: Child with me picked up an emblem

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted from bottom to top, so the word is read upwards

explanation.surface: A child and the speaker collect a badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' reverses ME to EM in this down clue; 'an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a natural object or animal adopted as the symbol of a clan, an emblem.

clue.text: Without leader, nearer failure

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: closer means nearer

explanation.surface: Getting close with no one in front still ends in defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is a person or thing that fails, so a failure.

clue.text: Cleaned out, son displayed sorrow

parts.note: to weep is to show sorrow; wept is its past tense

explanation.surface: A son cries after his room is emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: A room swept out has been brushed clean, so it has been cleaned out.

clue.text: Not an Irish county crop

indicators.note: not the following word, so those letters are left out of the county

parts.note: Antrim is a county in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A crop that is not grown in some county of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To crop hair or a hedge is to trim it, cut it short.

clue.text: An east European impressed by no French emperor

indicators.note: pressed into the other piece, so the European goes inside the French word

parts.note: non is French for no
a Pole is a person from Poland, in eastern Europe

explanation.surface: An Eastern European is left cold by a French ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressed' looks like admiration, but it means pressed inside: A POLE goes inside NON.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804.

clue.text: After a month, seek disguise

indicators.note: the request comes after the month, so its letters follow

parts.note: to seek is to ask for

explanation.surface: After a month of searching, someone goes looking for a disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A mask covers the face to hide identity, so it is a disguise.

clue.text: Uncontrolled teen lust is to cause restlessness

indicators.note: something uncontrolled runs wild, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Adolescent desire running wild is apt to make one agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncontrolled' rearranges TEEN LUST; 'is to' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle someone is to disturb or agitate them, making them uneasy and restless.
